question: In which of the following places did Mahatma Gandhi, along with other Indians, establish the Natal Congress to fight against racial discrimination?
solution_text:
The correct answer is South Africa.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Mahatma Gandhi, along with other Indians, established the Natal Indian Congress (NIC) in 1894 in South Africa to fight against racial discrimination faced by the Indian community. (नेटाल कांग्रेस — दक्षिण अफ्रीका)

 

• Gandhi had gone to South Africa in 1893 to work as a lawyer and witnessed severe racial discrimination against Indians there, which led him to organise the community politically.

 

• The Natal Indian Congress was modelled on the Indian National Congress and worked to protect the rights of the Indian diaspora in the British colony of Natal.

 

• Gandhi's experiences and activism in South Africa (1893-1914), including the development of the technique of Satyagraha, laid the foundation for his later leadership of the Indian freedom struggle.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Gandhi returned to India in 1915 and is regarded as the Father of the Nation; his South African phase is often called his political apprenticeship.

 

• The passive resistance movement he led in South Africa against the discriminatory Black Act (1906) was his first large-scale use of Satyagraha.

 

NOTE

 

• India (Option 2): Gandhi was already a well-known leader by the time he returned to India in 1915; the Natal Congress predates this period.

 

• England (Option 3): Gandhi studied law in England (1888-1891) but did not establish the Natal Congress there.

 

• France (Option 4): Gandhi had no such association with France during this period.

question: In February 2023, BVR Subrahmanyam was appointed as the ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is CEO NITI Ayog.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• B.V.R. Subrahmanyam, a retired IAS officer and former Union Commerce Secretary, was appointed as the CEO of NITI Aayog in February 2023. (नीति आयोग सीईओ — बीवीआर सुब्रमण्यम)

 

• He succeeded Parameswaran Iyer as CEO of NITI Aayog.

 

• NITI Aayog (National Institution for Transforming India) is the premier policy think tank of the Government of India, replacing the erstwhile Planning Commission in 2015.

 

• The CEO of NITI Aayog is appointed by the Prime Minister (who is the ex-officio Chairperson of NITI Aayog) and holds the rank of a Secretary to the Government of India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• NITI Aayog's Vice-Chairperson (a separate post) has been Suman Bery since 2022.

 

• NITI Aayog was formed on 1 January 2015 to foster cooperative federalism through structured support to states.

 

NOTE

 

• Chief Vigilance Commissioner (Option 1): This is a separate constitutional/statutory post heading the Central Vigilance Commission, unrelated to this appointment.

 

• Comptroller General Of India (Option 2): There is no such post by this exact name; the relevant post is the Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) of India.

 

• Chief Election Commissioner (Option 4): This post heads the Election Commission of India and was not the position BVR Subrahmanyam was appointed to.

question: Which type of well-managed industry was established in India at the time of independence?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Steel and Cotton.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• At the time of India's independence in 1947, the industrial sector was relatively well-developed only in the cotton textile and iron and steel industries. (लौह-इस्पात और सूती वस्त्र उद्योग — स्वतंत्रता के समय)

 

• The cotton textile industry had grown substantially during the colonial period, especially around Mumbai and Ahmedabad, using domestically produced raw cotton.

 

• The iron and steel industry had also begun to develop, most notably with the establishment of the Tata Iron and Steel Company (TISCO) at Jamshedpur in 1907.

 

• Most other modern industries — electronics, cement, sugar in an organised large scale, chemicals — were either absent or in a very nascent stage at independence.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The jute industry, concentrated in Bengal, was another relatively developed industry at independence.

 

• Post-independence Five Year Plans, starting 1951, focused heavily on building heavy industries such as steel (e.g., Bhilai, Rourkela, Durgapur plants) to diversify the industrial base.

 

NOTE

 

• Electronics and Electricals (Option 1): These were modern industries that developed largely after independence, not well established at the time of independence.

 

• Steel and Electronics (Option 2): While steel was developed, electronics was not an established industry at independence.

 

• Cement and Sugar (Option 4): These industries existed on a smaller scale but were not among the well-managed/well-developed industries at independence compared to steel and cotton.

question: Yakshagan is a folk dance of which of the following states?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Karnataka.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Yakshagana is a traditional folk theatre/dance form of Karnataka, combining dance, music, dialogue, costume, and elaborate make-up. (यक्षगान — कर्नाटक)

 

• It is particularly popular in the coastal and Malnad (Western Ghats) districts of Karnataka, such as Udupi, Dakshina Kannada, Uttara Kannada, and Shivamogga.

 

• Yakshagana performances traditionally depict stories from Hindu epics like the Ramayana and Mahabharata, and Puranas, performed through the night by torchlight in earlier times.

 

• Performers wear large, colourful headgear and costumes, and the narrative is driven by a Bhagavata (singer-narrator) accompanied by musicians and a chorus.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other major dance/folk forms of Karnataka include Dollu Kunitha (drum dance) and Veeragase.

 

• Yakshagana is sometimes referred to as the "Dance Drama of Karnataka" and has influenced Kannada literature and theatre significantly.

 

NOTE

 

• Odisha (Option 1): Known for classical dance Odissi and folk forms like Chhau (Mayurbhanj) and Gotipua, not Yakshagana.

 

• West Bengal (Option 2): Known for folk forms like Chhau (Purulia) and Baul music/dance, not Yakshagana.

 

• Madhya Pradesh (Option 3): Known for folk dances like Karma and Gaur, not Yakshagana.

question: Which of the following options best describes the primary cause of the per capita income decline?
option_4: Decline in the gross domestic product
solution_text:
The correct answer is Increase in the population growth.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Per capita income is calculated as Total National Income ÷ Total Population. When population grows faster than national income (GDP/GNI), per capita income declines even if total income is rising. (प्रति व्यक्ति आय गिरावट — जनसंख्या वृद्धि)

 

• A rapid increase in population growth dilutes the same total income among a larger number of people, thereby pulling down the average (per capita) income.

 

• This is a classic issue highlighted in the context of developing economies, where high population growth rates have historically offset gains in aggregate output, keeping per capita income low.

 

• Conversely, a decline in population growth (with income constant or rising) would tend to raise, not lower, per capita income.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's decadal population growth rate has been steadily declining since the 1990s due to falling fertility rates, which has helped per capita income grow faster than in earlier decades.

 

• Per capita income is a key, though imperfect, indicator of a country's standard of living, as it does not capture income distribution.

 

NOTE

 

• Equitable distribution of income (Option 1): This affects income inequality, not the overall level of per capita income, which is an average measure.

 

• Decline in the population growth (Option 3): This would, all else equal, raise per capita income rather than cause it to decline.

 

• Decline in the gross domestic product (Option 4): While a GDP decline can reduce per capita income, the question asks for the primary/typical cause, which relates to population growth outpacing income growth, not a shrinking economy.

question: Which television channel presents the IMMIES Awards every year with an aim to reward the best talent in the Indian music industry?
solution_text:
The correct answer is MTV.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The MTV Immies (Indian Music Awards) is an annual awards show presented by MTV India, honouring the best talent in the Indian music industry. (एमटीवी इमीज़ — भारतीय संगीत पुरस्कार)

 

• The Immies were launched by MTV India and covered categories across Bollywood, indi-pop, and regional Indian music.

 

• MTV, originally an American cable channel (Music Television), entered India in the 1990s and became a major platform for youth-oriented music and pop culture programming.

 

• Award shows like the Immies helped popularise and recognise emerging Indian music talent alongside established artists.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other Indian music channels include B4U Music, Channel V, and 9XM, which run their own music-related programming and countdown shows.

 

• MTV India has also produced other popular award/reality shows such as MTV Roadies and MTV Splitsvilla.

 

NOTE

 

• B4U Music (Option 1): A Bollywood/Hindi music channel; it does not present the IMMIES Awards.

 

• Channel V (Option 3): A youth entertainment channel known for music countdown shows, not the IMMIES.

 

• 9XM (Option 4): A Hindi music channel; it is not associated with the IMMIES Awards.

question: The first Indian Olympic Games was hosted by which of the following cities?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lahore.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The first Indian Olympic Games (the precursor to India's National Games) were held in Lahore in 1924 (then part of undivided British India). (प्रथम भारतीय ओलंपिक खेल — लाहौर)

 

• These games were organised to select and prepare Indian athletes and to promote the Olympic movement within the country ahead of India's participation in the international Olympics.

 

• The event is regarded as a forerunner of what later became the National Games of India, which continued and were renamed after independence.

 

• The Indian Olympic Association (IOA), formally established in 1927, went on to govern Olympic participation and related national sporting events for India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• India made its Olympic debut at the 1900 Paris Olympics and has participated regularly since the 1920 Antwerp Olympics.

 

• The National Games of India (rebranded from the Indian Olympic Games) are now held periodically in various Indian states/cities as a multi-sport event.

 

NOTE

 

• Madras (Option 2): Not the venue of the first Indian Olympic Games, though it has hosted other sporting events historically.

 

• Bombay (Option 3): Not the venue of the first Indian Olympic Games.

 

• Allahabad (Option 4): Not the venue of the first Indian Olympic Games.

question: Pushyabhuti dynasty, after Prabhakarvardhana, strengthened its position in the regions of Punjab and Haryana after defeating which of the following dynasties?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Hunas.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Prabhakarvardhana, the ruler of the Pushyabhuti (Vardhana) dynasty and father of Harshavardhana, strengthened the dynasty's position in Punjab and Haryana by defeating the Hunas. (पुष्यभूति वंश — हूणों की पराजय)

 

• Prabhakarvardhana is described in contemporary sources (such as Banabhatta's Harshacharita) as a "lion to the Huna deer" (Hunaharina Kesari), reflecting his military success against the Hunas.

 

• The Pushyabhuti dynasty was originally based at Thanesar (Sthanvishvara) in present-day Haryana, and its power expanded significantly under Prabhakarvardhana and later his son Harshavardhana.

 

• The defeat of the Hunas helped secure the north-western frontier regions (Punjab and Haryana) for the Vardhana kingdom.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Harshavardhana (606-647 CE), son of Prabhakarvardhana, later became one of the most powerful rulers of northern India, with his capital at Kannauj.

 

• The Hunas (Alchon Huns / White Huns) had invaded India in the 5th-6th centuries CE and were also earlier checked by Gupta rulers like Skandagupta.

 

NOTE

 

• Maukharis (Option 1): A contemporaneous dynasty based at Kannauj; the Vardhanas had a matrimonial alliance with them (Harsha's sister Rajyashri married the Maukhari king Grahavarman), not a military conquest in this context.

 

• Chalukyas (Option 3): A dynasty of the Deccan; Harshavardhana was later defeated by the Chalukya king Pulakeshin II on the Narmada, unrelated to Prabhakarvardhana's Punjab-Haryana campaigns.

 

• Maitrakas (Option 4): A dynasty that ruled in Gujarat (Vallabhi), not connected to this event.

question: Which law states that endothermic animals from cold climates have smaller extremities or appendages than closely related species from warm climates?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Allen's rule.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Allen's rule, formulated by American zoologist Joel Asaph Allen in 1877, states that endothermic (warm-blooded) animals from colder climates tend to have smaller extremities/appendages (ears, limbs, tails, snouts) than closely related species from warmer climates. (एलन का नियम — ठंडी जलवायु में छोटे अंग)

 

• The underlying principle is heat conservation: smaller appendages reduce the body's surface-area-to-volume ratio, minimising heat loss in cold environments.

 

• Conversely, animals in hot climates evolve larger appendages (e.g., large ears) to maximise heat dissipation and stay cool.

 

• A classic example is comparing Arctic foxes (small ears/short legs) with Fennec foxes of hot deserts (large ears, longer legs).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• A related ecogeographical rule is Bergmann's rule, which states that within a species/genus, populations in colder climates tend to be larger in body size than those in warmer climates, again for heat-conservation reasons.

 

• Both Allen's and Bergmann's rules are examples of adaptive evolutionary responses to climatic conditions.

 

NOTE

 

• Harper's rule (Option 1): Not a recognised ecological/biological rule relevant to this concept.

 

• Reich's rule (Option 2): Not a recognised ecological/biological rule relevant to this concept.

 

• Moller's rule (Option 4): Not a recognised ecological/biological rule relevant to this concept.

question: UPSC is a Constitutional Body to conduct examinations for appointments to the services of the Union and the services of the State, respectively, under Article ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 320.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 320 of the Indian Constitution lays down the functions of the Public Service Commissions, including the UPSC, such as conducting examinations for appointments to services of the Union and, where requested, the services of States. (अनुच्छेद 320 — संघ लोक सेवा आयोग के कार्य)

 

• The Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) is established under Article 315 of the Constitution as an independent constitutional body.

 

• Under Article 320, the UPSC is consulted on matters like recruitment methods, conditions of service, promotions, transfers, and disciplinary matters relating to civil servants.

 

• UPSC conducts major examinations such as the Civil Services Examination (CSE), Engineering Services Examination, and others for All-India and Central Services.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Articles 315 to 323 in Part XIV of the Constitution deal with the Public Service Commissions (Union and State).

 

• The Chairman and Members of the UPSC are appointed by the President of India and can be removed only through a process involving the Supreme Court under Article 317.

 

NOTE

 

• Article 324 (Option 2): Provides for the Election Commission of India and superintendence, direction and control of elections.

 

• Article 328 (Option 3): Empowers State Legislatures to make provisions regarding elections to that State's legislature.

 

• Article 332 (Option 4): Provides for reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in State Legislative Assemblies.

question: Which of the following states suffers from ‘Loo’?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rajasthan.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• 'Loo' refers to the strong, hot, dry, dust-laden winds that blow across the north and north-western plains of India, including Rajasthan, during the summer months (April-June). (लू — राजस्थान की गर्म हवाएं)

 

• Rajasthan, being part of the hot, arid north-western region, experiences intense Loo conditions with daytime temperatures often exceeding 45°C during peak summer.

 

• Loo winds typically blow from the west/north-west towards the east during the day and can cause heatstroke and dehydration in people exposed to them.

 

• Other states affected by Loo include Punjab, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, and Bihar, but Rajasthan is among the most severely affected due to its hot desert climate.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Thar Desert, located mostly in Rajasthan, contributes to the extreme summer heat and the intensity of Loo winds in the region.

 

• In contrast, coastal and north-eastern states experience a more moderate summer climate due to maritime influence or higher humidity/rainfall.

 

NOTE

 

• Karnataka (Option 1): A southern peninsular state with a moderate climate influenced by both coast and plateau; not known for Loo.

 

• Kerala (Option 2): A coastal state with a humid tropical climate; not affected by Loo.

 

• Assam (Option 3): A north-eastern state with a humid subtropical climate and heavy rainfall; not affected by Loo.

question: Pandit Ram Narayan was associated with which of the following musical instruments?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sarangi.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Pandit Ram Narayan was a legendary Indian classical musician renowned for establishing the Sarangi as a solo concert instrument. (पंडित राम नारायण — सारंगी)

 

• He is widely credited with elevating the Sarangi from an accompanying instrument (traditionally used to accompany vocalists and Kathak dancers) to a respected solo instrument in Hindustani classical music.

 

• He was honoured with India's civilian awards, including the Padma Vibhushan (2005), for his contribution to classical music.

 

• The Sarangi is a bowed, short-necked string instrument known for its close resemblance to the human voice.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other renowned Sarangi players include Ustad Sultan Khan and Pandit Ramesh Mishra.

 

• Ram Narayan's contributions helped popularise Hindustani classical instrumental music internationally through his solo Sarangi recitals and recordings.

 

NOTE

 

• Sarod (Option 1): Associated with maestros like Ustad Ali Akbar Khan and Amjad Ali Khan, not Ram Narayan.

 

• Rudra veena (Option 2): Associated with players like the Dagar family (Dhrupad tradition), not Ram Narayan.

 

• Mohan veena (Option 4): A modern slide guitar-based instrument associated with Pandit Vishwa Mohan Bhatt, not Ram Narayan.

question: The Tripartite struggle happened among the Palas, the Pratiharas and the _______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rashtrakutas.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Tripartite Struggle was a prolonged three-way conflict for control of Kannauj (a strategically important city in the Gangetic plains) between the Palas of Bengal, the Gurjara-Pratiharas of western/northern India, and the Rashtrakutas of the Deccan, from roughly the 8th to 10th centuries CE. (त्रिपक्षीय संघर्ष — पाल, प्रतिहार, राष्ट्रकूट)

 

• The struggle was primarily about controlling Kannauj, which symbolised imperial sovereignty over northern India at the time.

 

• Key rulers involved included Dharmapala and Devapala (Palas), Nagabhata II and Mihira Bhoja (Pratiharas), and Dhruva, Govinda III, and Indra III (Rashtrakutas).

 

• Ultimately, the prolonged conflict weakened all three powers and contributed to the eventual decline of centralised authority in northern India, paving the way for regional kingdoms.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Rashtrakutas, based at Manyakheta (Malkhed) in present-day Karnataka, were also great patrons of art and architecture, notably the Kailasa Temple at Ellora.

 

• The Gurjara-Pratiharas, based at Kannauj, are also remembered for resisting early Arab invasions from the west.

 

NOTE

 

• Chandelas (Option 1): A dynasty of Central India (Bundelkhand), famous for the Khajuraho temples, not part of the Tripartite Struggle.

 

• Maukharis (Option 2): An earlier dynasty based at Kannauj (6th century CE), predating the Tripartite Struggle period.

 

• Chalukyas (Option 4): A separate Deccan dynasty, rivals of the Rashtrakutas, but not one of the three main contenders in the Tripartite Struggle.

question: Guru Ghasidas led which of the following movements to improve the social condition of leather workers in British India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Satnami Movement.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Guru Ghasidas founded the Satnami Movement in the early 19th century (around 1820) in the Chhattisgarh region to improve the social and religious condition of the Chamars (leather workers), who faced severe caste-based discrimination. (सतनामी आंदोलन — गुरु घासीदास)

 

• The movement preached belief in one formless God (Satnam, meaning "true name") and rejected idol worship, caste distinctions, and superstitions.

 

• It gave the Chamar community of Chhattisgarh a sense of social identity, dignity, and religious unity, encouraging simple living and moral conduct.

 

• Guru Ghasidas is revered as a social reformer among the Satnami community, and his teachings continue to influence the religious life of the region.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Satnami sect is distinct from the earlier North Indian Satnami sect founded by Guru Jagjivan Das in the 17th century, though both share the core belief in Satnam.

 

• Guru Ghasidas's birthplace, Girod village in Chhattisgarh, remains an important pilgrimage site for the Satnami community.

 

NOTE

 

• Aravipuram Movement (Option 1): Led by Sree Narayana Guru in Kerala for the upliftment of the Ezhava community, not related to Guru Ghasidas.

 

• Satyashodhak Samaj (Option 2): Founded by Jyotirao Phule in Maharashtra (1873) to fight caste discrimination, unrelated to Guru Ghasidas.

 

• Nirankari Movement (Option 3): Founded by Baba Dyal Das in Punjab, a Sikh reform movement, unrelated to Guru Ghasidas.

question: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT regarding water remaining colder in an earthen pot (matka)?
option_1: Water gets evaporated at the surface of the earthen pot.
option_3: Environmental water vapour enters the pot through pores.
option_4: The water oozes out through the pores in an earthen pot.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Environmental water vapour enters the pot through pores.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• An earthen pot (matka) keeps water cool through the principle of evaporative cooling. Because the pot is porous, water from inside slowly oozes out through the tiny pores to the outer surface. (मटके का जल शीतलन — वाष्पीकरण)

 

• This water on the outer surface evaporates into the surrounding air, and evaporation requires latent heat, which is drawn from the remaining water inside the pot.

 

• As heat is continuously drawn away for evaporation, the temperature of the water remaining inside the pot drops, keeping it cooler than the ambient temperature.

 

• The statement that "environmental water vapour enters the pot through the pores" describes the process in the wrong direction — it is the pot's own water that moves outward through the pores to evaporate, not atmospheric vapour moving inward; hence this statement is INCORRECT.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• This cooling effect works best in hot, dry (low-humidity) climates, where evaporation from the pot's surface is faster; it is far less effective in humid conditions.

 

• The same principle of evaporative cooling is used in devices like desert/evaporative air coolers.

 

NOTE

 

• Water gets evaporated at the surface of the earthen pot (Option 1): This is correct — evaporation from the outer surface is precisely what cools the water inside.

 

• The earthen pot is porous (Option 2): This is correct — porosity is essential; it allows water to seep out to the surface.

 

• The water oozes out through the pores in an earthen pot (Option 4): This is correct — this outward seepage is what supplies water to the surface for evaporation.

question: Each of the following statements includes two terms. In three cases, the two terms mean the same as each other. In which of the following cases do the two terms NOT mean the same as each other?
option_1: Nominal GDP and GDP at current prices
option_2: The base period and the reference period
option_3: Changes in real GDP and the GDP deflator
option_4: Real GDP and GDP at constant prices
solution_text:
The correct answer is Changes in real GDP and the GDP deflator.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Real GDP measures output valued at constant (base year) prices, so changes in real GDP reflect changes in the physical quantity/volume of output produced. (सकल घरेलू उत्पाद अपस्फीतिकारक — वास्तविक जीडीपी से भिन्न)

 

• The GDP deflator, on the other hand, is a price index calculated as (Nominal GDP ÷ Real GDP) × 100, and it measures changes in the general price level of goods and services in the economy.

 

• Since one measures quantity change (real GDP) and the other measures price change (GDP deflator), "changes in real GDP" and "the GDP deflator" are conceptually different, not synonymous terms.

 

• In contrast, the other three pairs listed are genuinely synonymous term-pairs used interchangeably in national income accounting.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Nominal GDP is GDP calculated at prevailing (current) market prices, i.e., it is identical in meaning to "GDP at current prices."

 

• The base year (the reference year against which real GDP/index numbers are calculated) is also referred to as the reference period in national accounts terminology.

 

NOTE

 

• Nominal GDP and GDP at current prices (Option 1): These are synonymous — both refer to GDP valued using current-year prices.

 

• The base period and the reference period (Option 2): These are synonymous — both refer to the fixed year used as the benchmark for comparison.

 

• Real GDP and GDP at constant prices (Option 4): These are synonymous — both refer to GDP valued using base-year (constant) prices to remove the effect of price changes.

question: What is the unit of specific resistance?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ohm meter.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Specific resistance, also called electrical resistivity (ρ), is a material property that quantifies how strongly a material opposes the flow of electric current. Its SI unit is the ohm-metre (Ω·m). (विशिष्ट प्रतिरोध — ओम-मीटर)

 

• Resistivity is defined by the relation R = ρ (L/A), where R is resistance, L is length, and A is the cross-sectional area of the conductor; rearranging gives ρ = RA/L, whose unit works out to ohm-metre.

 

• Resistivity is an intrinsic property of a material (depends on the material and temperature) and does not depend on the object's dimensions, unlike resistance itself.

 

• Good conductors like copper and silver have very low resistivity, while insulators have very high resistivity.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The reciprocal of resistivity is electrical conductivity, measured in siemens per metre (S/m).

 

• Resistivity generally increases with temperature for metals (conductors) and decreases with temperature for semiconductors.

 

NOTE

 

• Farad (Option 1): This is the SI unit of capacitance, not resistivity.

 

• Ampere (Option 2): This is the SI unit of electric current, not resistivity.

 

• Coulomb (Option 3): This is the SI unit of electric charge, not resistivity.

question: The National Youth Policy 2014 defines youth as population between the ages of ________ and _________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 15; 29.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The National Youth Policy (NYP) 2014, launched by the Government of India, defines "youth" as persons in the age group of 15 to 29 years. (राष्ट्रीय युवा नीति 2014 — 15-29 वर्ष)

 

• This was a change from the earlier National Youth Policy, 2003, which had defined youth as those aged 13 to 35 years.

 

• The NYP 2014 is administered by the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports and aims at the holistic development of youth, focusing on areas such as education, employment, skill development, health, and social values.

 

• As per the policy, India's youth in the 15-29 age bracket constitute a very large share (about 27.5%) of the country's total population, making youth-centric policy especially significant ("demographic dividend").

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The NYP 2014 identifies five priority areas: Education; Employment & Skill Development; Health & Healthy Lifestyle; Sports; and Promotion of Social Values.

 

• India is often described as having one of the youngest populations in the world, which underpins several flagship skilling and employment schemes.

 

NOTE

 

• 20; 29 (Option 1): Not the age range defined by NYP 2014.

 

• 15; 25 (Option 2): Not the age range defined by NYP 2014.

 

• 10; 19 (Option 4): This range roughly corresponds to WHO's definition of "adolescents," not the NYP 2014 definition of youth.

question: What gave a major impetus to the cotton textile industry in India after Independence?
option_2: Export of raw cotton to England
solution_text:
The correct answer is Swadeshi movement.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Swadeshi Movement, which encouraged Indians to boycott foreign (especially British) goods and use indigenously manufactured products, gave a major and lasting impetus to the growth of the cotton textile industry in India. (स्वदेशी आंदोलन — सूती वस्त्र उद्योग को प्रोत्साहन)

 

• By fostering a strong sense of national pride and self-reliance, the movement significantly boosted domestic demand for Indian-made cotton textiles and reduced dependence on British imports.

 

• This increased demand encouraged the establishment of new textile mills across India (notably in Bombay and Ahmedabad) and supported the sustained expansion of the industry over subsequent decades, including after independence.

 

• The Swadeshi spirit, first prominent during the 1905 anti-partition agitation in Bengal, continued to shape economic policy and consumer preference in independent India's early industrial development.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The cotton textile industry remains one of India's oldest and largest organised industries, concentrated historically in Maharashtra and Gujarat.

 

• Post-independence, India also promoted khadi and handloom production as an extension of the Swadeshi ideals through institutions like the Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC).

 

NOTE

 

• Partition of India in 1947 (Option 1): The partition actually disrupted the cotton textile industry, since many cotton-growing areas went to Pakistan while most mills remained in India, creating raw material shortages rather than giving impetus.

 

• Export of raw cotton to England (Option 2): This was a colonial-era practice that drained raw material away from Indian mills and benefited British industry, not the Indian cotton textile industry.

 

• Development of railway network (Option 4): While railways aided overall industrial transport and growth, they were not the primary or specific driver credited for boosting the cotton textile industry.

question: Which of the following is a key focus area of the ‘Amrit Dharohar’ scheme launched by the Prime Minister Narendra Modi on World Environment Day, 2023?
option_1: Preservation of ancient Indian heritage sites
option_3: To promote values of local communities in conserving wetland ecosystem
solution_text:
The correct answer is To promote values of local communities in conserving wetland ecosystem.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The 'Amrit Dharohar' scheme, announced by the Government of India, is aimed at encouraging the optimal use of wetlands and promoting the conservation values, unique biodiversity, and ecological importance of wetlands, with active involvement of local communities. (अमृत धरोहर योजना — आर्द्रभूमि संरक्षण)

 

• The scheme envisages developing wetlands as sites for eco-tourism, promoting biodiversity conservation, and generating livelihood and income opportunities for local communities living around wetland areas.

 

• It is implemented under the Ramsar Convention framework, complementing India's push to have more of its wetlands recognised as Ramsar sites of international importance.

 

• The scheme was first announced in the Union Budget 2023-24, and its focus was subsequently reiterated and highlighted around key environmental observances of 2023.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• India significantly expanded its Ramsar wetland sites in 2022-2023, taking the total count to over 75 Ramsar sites, the highest in South Asia.

 

• The MISHTI scheme (Mangrove Initiative for Shoreline Habitats & Tangible Incomes), announced in the same budget, is a related initiative focused on mangrove conservation.

 

NOTE

 

• Preservation of ancient Indian heritage sites (Option 1): This is not the focus of Amrit Dharohar, which is specifically about wetland ecosystems, not archaeological/heritage monuments.

 

• Development of rural infrastructure (Option 2): This is a broad, unrelated policy area and not the specific aim of this scheme.

 

• Promotion of organic farming (Option 4): This is addressed by separate schemes (e.g., PM-PRANAM, PKVY) and is not the focus of Amrit Dharohar.

question: Subansiri, Jia Bharali, Dhansiri and Puthimari are the major tributaries of which river?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Brahmaputra.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Subansiri, Jia Bharali (Kameng), Dhansiri, and Puthimari are major right-bank/north-bank tributaries of the Brahmaputra river, which flows through Assam. (सुबनसिरी, जिया भराली — ब्रह्मपुत्र की सहायक नदियां)

 

• The Subansiri is the largest tributary of the Brahmaputra by discharge, originating in Tibet and flowing through Arunachal Pradesh before joining the Brahmaputra in Assam.

 

• The Brahmaputra river system has numerous tributaries from both the north (Himalayan) and south (hilly) sides, contributing to it being one of India's largest and most powerful rivers by discharge.

 

• Other notable tributaries of the Brahmaputra include the Manas, Teesta (via some classifications), Dibang, and Lohit rivers.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Brahmaputra originates as the Yarlung Tsangpo in Tibet, enters India through Arunachal Pradesh, flows through Assam, and then into Bangladesh, where it is called the Jamuna before merging with the Ganga.

 

• The Brahmaputra is known for causing frequent and severe flooding in Assam due to its heavy sediment load and braided channel pattern.

 

NOTE

 

• Godavari (Option 1): A major peninsular river of South India; its tributaries include the Pranhita, Indravati, and Manjira, not the ones listed.

 

• Mahanadi (Option 2): A river flowing through Chhattisgarh and Odisha; its tributaries include the Seonath and Hasdeo, not the ones listed.

 

• Bhagirathi (Option 4): A Himalayan headstream of the Ganga in Uttarakhand; it is not associated with these tributaries.

question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution mentions about the ‘Promotion of educational and economic interests of Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes and other weaker sections’?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 46.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 46 of the Indian Constitution, under the Directive Principles of State Policy (Part IV), directs the State to promote with special care the educational and economic interests of the weaker sections of society, particularly the Scheduled Castes (SCs) and the Scheduled Tribes (STs), and to protect them from social injustice and exploitation. (अनुच्छेद 46 — अनुसूचित जाति/जनजाति के शैक्षिक व आर्थिक हित)

 

• This provision reflects the constitutional commitment to social justice and affirmative action for historically disadvantaged and marginalised communities.

 

• Article 46 has served as the constitutional basis for various welfare schemes, reservations in education and employment, and targeted development programmes for SC/ST communities.

 

• Being a Directive Principle, Article 46 is not directly enforceable by courts but is fundamental to the governance of the country and guides State policy-making.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Directive Principles of State Policy (Articles 36-51) are non-justiciable guidelines aimed at establishing social and economic democracy, complementing the Fundamental Rights.

 

• Related provisions include Article 15(4) and Article 16(4), which enable the State to make special provisions/reservations for SCs, STs, and other backward classes.

 

NOTE

 

• Article 45 (Option 1): Originally dealt with provision for free and compulsory education for children (now largely covered by Article 21A); currently deals with early childhood care and education.

 

• Article 48 (Option 2): Deals with the organisation of agriculture and animal husbandry, including preservation of livestock breeds and prohibition of cow slaughter.

 

• Article 47 (Option 3): Deals with the State's duty to raise the level of nutrition, standard of living, and improve public health.

question: Vishu festival is celebrated in which of the following states?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kerala And Tamil Nadu.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Vishu is a harvest festival marking the traditional solar new year, celebrated principally in Kerala and also observed in parts of Tamil Nadu. (विशु त्यौहार — केरल और तमिलनाडु)

 

• It typically falls around 14 April, coinciding with the start of the Malayalam month of Medam, and follows the solar (not lunar) calendar.

 

• A central ritual of Vishu is the 'Vishukkani' — an auspicious arrangement of items (rice, fruits, flowers, gold, a mirror, etc.) that family members view first thing in the morning, believed to bring good fortune for the year ahead.

 

• In Tamil Nadu, a corresponding solar new year festival, Puthandu, is celebrated around the same time with similar customs of new beginnings and prosperity.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other Indian regional/solar new year festivals celebrated around mid-April include Baisakhi (Punjab), Bihu (Assam), Poila Boishakh (West Bengal), and Puthandu (Tamil Nadu).

 

• 'Vishukkaineettam' (giving money as a gift, usually by elders to youngsters) is another important Vishu tradition symbolising blessings for prosperity.

 

NOTE

 

• Kerala And Karnataka (Option 1): While some Tulu-speaking areas of coastal Karnataka observe related customs, the standard association for Vishu is Kerala and Tamil Nadu.

 

• Madhya Pradesh & Rajasthan (Option 3): These states do not traditionally celebrate Vishu.

 

• Gujarat and Maharashtra (Option 4): These states do not traditionally celebrate Vishu; they follow their own new year observances (e.g., Gudi Padwa in Maharashtra).

question: At which Olympic games did Abhinav Bindra win the gold medal?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Beijing 2008.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Abhinav Bindra won the gold medal in the Men's 10m Air Rifle shooting event at the 2008 Beijing Olympics, becoming the first Indian to win an individual Olympic gold medal. (अभिनव बिंद्रा — बीजिंग ओलंपिक 2008 स्वर्ण पदक)

 

• This historic win made Bindra the first Indian to achieve an individual gold medal at the Olympic Games, a landmark moment in Indian sporting history.

 

• Before this, Indian gold medals at the Olympics had come only in field hockey (team events), most notably the multiple golds won prior to 1980.

 

• Bindra was honoured with India's highest sporting award, the Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna, and later the civilian award Padma Bhushan.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's next individual Olympic gold after Bindra came at the 2020 Tokyo Olympics (held in 2021), when Neeraj Chopra won gold in the Javelin Throw.

 

• Abhinav Bindra also won a bronze medal in shooting at the 2020 Tokyo Youth Olympics mentoring role aside, and remains a prominent figure in Indian sports administration and mentorship.

 

NOTE

 

• Athens 2004 (Option 1): Bindra competed here but did not win a medal at this edition.

 

• Rio 2016 (Option 2): Bindra competed here in his final Olympics but did not win a medal.

 

• London 2012 (Option 4): Bindra competed here but did not win a medal at this edition.

question: Which of the following organisations is associated with the development of the web version: e-GOPALA application?
option_4: National Institute of Agricultural Extension Management
solution_text:
The correct answer is National Dairy Development Board (NDDB).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The web version of the e-GOPALA application was developed by the National Dairy Development Board (NDDB), under the Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying. (ई-गोपाला ऐप — राष्ट्रीय डेयरी विकास बोर्ड)

 

• e-GOPALA is a comprehensive breed improvement and farmer-centric mobile/web application that provides livestock farmers with information on nutrition, animal health, and best practices for livestock management.

 

• Along with e-GOPALA's web version, NDDB also developed the IMAP (Information Network for Animal Productivity and Health) web portal to further support livestock-related data management.

 

• NDDB, headquartered in Anand, Gujarat, was established in 1965 and is the apex body promoting cooperative dairy development in India, closely associated with India's 'White Revolution.'

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• NDDB played a central role in 'Operation Flood', launched in 1970, which transformed India into the world's largest milk producer.

 

• The e-GOPALA app also helps farmers access artificial insemination services, information on government schemes, and marketplace features for buying/selling animals.

 

NOTE

 

• Indian Council of Agricultural Research (Option 2): ICAR is India's apex body for agricultural research and education but was not the developer of the e-GOPALA web version.

 

• National Dairy Research Institute (Option 3): NDRI is a premier dairy research institute (Karnal) but is not credited with developing the e-GOPALA web version.

 

• National Institute of Agricultural Extension Management (Option 4): MANAGE focuses on agricultural extension training and management, and was not the developer of e-GOPALA.
